subject: english
question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

Young scientists have fresh ideas; they are ambitious and highly productive.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'No error'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically correct.
 
• Here, everything is correctly used.
 
• We know that after '**plural**' subject **a plural helping verb** is used. Here, '**have**' is used which is completely correct.
 
• And in the second clause after '**they**' '**are**' is used which is also correct.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *Young scientists have fresh ideas; they are ambitious and highly productive.* 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **__Confusion Points__**

 
• The **adverb **"**highly**" is correctly used in the sentence.
 
• In English, adverbs can modify verbs, adjectives, and other adverbs.
 
• In the phrase "**highly productive**," "**highly**" is an adverb that modifies the adjective "**productive**."
 
• This is a common and** grammatically correct** usage.
